title: Cube boundary fraction and total influence
statement: Let $n>0$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Choose uniformly an undirected edge of the $n$-dimensional cube, and let the boundary fraction be the probability that the endpoints receive different values under $f$. Then this fraction equals the total influence of $f$, defined as the sum over coordinates of the uniform average of the squared discrete derivative, divided by $n$.
